name: Arco de la Victoria (Moncloa)
story: This 40 m triumphal arch at the entrance to the University City was built in 1950–56 to commemorate the Francoist victory in the battle for the University City, where the front ran from November 1936 to March 1939. Its Latin inscriptions praise Franco's army and the rebuilt university. Since the Democratic Memory laws it has been the subject of debate over re-naming and re-signification; the avenue beneath it was renamed Avenida de la Concordia in 2024.
see: The arch itself, seen from the Moncloa interchange; it cannot be entered.
plan: View from outside, beside Metro Moncloa; combine with the University City and the Parque del Oeste.
